title: The Second Letter of John Timeline
sub: Truth, Love, and a Warning at the Door
desc: John's shortest surviving letter, likely addressed to a specific house church, warning against giving hospitality to traveling teachers who deny that Jesus came in the flesh.

eras.label: Era One · 2 John 1
eras.name: Truth, Love, and a Warning at the Door
eras.dates: The shortest of John's letters, likely written to a specific house church addressed as an 'elect lady,' warning against giving deceivers a welcome

events.title: Greeting to the Elect Lady
events.detail: The elder writes to an 'elect lady and her children' — likely a coded way of addressing a specific local church and its members — grounding the letter in truth that abides permanently.

verses.text: “The elder to the elect lady and her children, whom I love in truth, and not only I, but also all who know the truth.”

events.title: Walking in Truth and Love — An Old Commandment
events.detail: John rejoices at some of the community walking in truth, then restates the same command found throughout his first letter: not a new rule, but the original call to love one another by walking according to God's commandments.

verses.text: “This is love, that we walk according to His commandments. This is the commandment, just as you have heard from the beginning, that you should walk in it.”

events.title: Beware Deceivers — Do Not Welcome the Antichrist's Teaching
events.detail: The letter's real occasion: deceivers denying Jesus came in the flesh are circulating, and John gives a blunt practical instruction — don't receive such a teacher into your house or even greet him, since doing so shares in his evil work.

verses.text: “If anyone comes to you and does not bring this teaching, do not receive him into your house, and do not give him a greeting, for the one who gives him a greeting participates in his evil deeds.”

events.title: Closing — Paper and Ink, or Face to Face
events.detail: John cuts the letter short, preferring to say the rest in person rather than trust it to paper and ink — closing with greetings from the children of the recipient's 'elect sister,' another likely coded reference to a sister congregation.

verses.text: “Though I have many things to write to you, I do not want to do so with paper and ink; but I hope to come to you and speak face to face, so that your joy may be made complete.”
